_readme: Union on 24th, 701 W 24th St, as js/slopes-apartments.js draws it. An H-plan tower: a five-level podium filling the whole site behind a dark fin screen over a recessed glazed ground floor, and above it two 23-storey wings joined by a central bar, with a court cut clean through and open at BOTH ends - north on to W 24th St and south on to the amenity level. Metres in the footprint's oriented bounding box (js/westcampus.js obbOf): L=80.1, W=55.0. u=0 is the EAST end (Rio Grande St) and +u runs WEST; v=0 is the NORTH (W 24th St) edge and +v runs SOUTH. THE MEASUREMENT SOURCE IS S2, the hand-built three.js model - every massing number below is ported from it with the line it came from. Read docs/apartments.md for the schema.
name: Union on 24th

sources.S1: data/snapshots/2026-08-27/buildings.detailed.geojson feature 0a6d10a2-a664-4049-9ea2-83ce692103ef: name 'Union on 24th', num_floors 29, final_height 97.5, source_height 'overture' - a guess for a building OSM never tagged with a height. The footprint is a clean 4-vertex rectangle, 79.98 x 55.01 m (4,404 m2), long axis at bearing 275.1 deg.
sources.S2: C:/Users/simip/Projects/utx-diorama/workbench/js/union.js - the owner's hand-built three.js model of THIS building, v7/v8, built to utx-diorama/docs/UNION24_AUDIT.md and adversarially re-measured over several passes. It is the measurement source for every dimension here: the H plan, the square 3.26 m facade module, the 5-level podium, the 23 residential rows, the mod-4 cell fractions, the court's three wall systems, the podium fin screen and its band rhythm, the L29 grill pavilion, and every material hex. Each number below cites the constant or the line it was ported from.
sources.S3: js/union24.js in this repo - the same measurements already applied to the flat Overture prism (envelope 25.18 MOD, depth 16 MOD, wing 7 MOD, south court 5 MOD, north court 6 MOD, parapet 94.4 m, distant wall read #6f7172). This file is the mesh version of that; the prism it replaces is that H.
sources.S4: data/roads.geojson - the unnamed east-west way at lat 30.2880 spanning the building's full width immediately north of it is W 24th St, and Rio Grande St runs north-south along the building's east edge. That is what fixes which end of the obb is which, and it agrees with S2's note that the north court 'opens north, onto W 24th'.
sources.S5: skyscraperpage for 701 W 24th St, quoted in S2's first line: 94.5 m over 29 stories, i.e. FLOOR = 3.26 m. S2 makes that floor height the square facade module, verified four ways there.
sources.S6: OSM way 1208654798 - the outline S1's polygon comes from; no height, no levels, no building:part.
sources.S7: Google Earth 3D at an oblique over West Campus, captured headless with scripts/verify/chrome.mjs on the hardware GL backend and page.screenshot() - used only to place and check the massing against the photogrammetry mesh, never to measure it.

footprint._src: S1 verbatim. In (u,v) the four corners are (0,0) (79.98,0) (80.05,55.01) (0.06,55.01) - the polygon IS its own oriented bounding box, so every edge is axis-parallel in the frame.

_frame_src: obbOf(ring): L=80.05, W=55.01, +u at bearing 275.1 deg, so +u runs WEST and u=0 is the east (Rio Grande St) end; +v is 90 deg counter-clockwise from +u in (east, north), i.e. SOUTH, so v=0 is the north (W 24th St) edge (S4). S3 reads the same quad's edges as a long axis at 95.2 deg, which is the same line taken the other way.
_massing_src: HOW S2's NUMBERS LAND IN THIS FOOTPRINT, and the one place they disagree. S2 builds the tower outward from the square 3.26 m module: depth 16 MOD = 52.16 m N-S, each wing 7 MOD = 22.82 m, and a podium apron oversailing the tower by 1.5 m on every side. This footprint is 80.05 x 55.01 m. Take S2's 1.5 m apron off the traced outline and the tower depth comes out 52.01 m against S2's 52.16 - agreement to 0.15 m, which independently confirms BOTH the 1.5 m apron and the 3.26 m module, and says the traced outline is the podium apron, not the tower. E-W the same subtraction gives a 77.05 m tower against S2's 82.09, a real 5 m disagreement: S2's E-W is a photograph chain (a cap measured at 7.007 bays in one plane, a court gap at 11.18 MOD), the outline is a traced polygon. The traced outline wins here because everything else in this app is keyed to it and because the N-S agreement shows the trace is good to 0.15 m on the axis where the two can be compared. So: wings stay at the frozen 7 x 3.26 = 22.82 m, and the court absorbs the difference at 31.41 m instead of S2's 36.45 m. That makes the court back wall 10 bays where S2 counted 12 - written down in `open`, not papered over.

levels._src: FLOOR = 3.26 m (S5, S2's first constant). 0 is grade and 4.40 is the top of the recessed ground floor (S2 H1 = 4.4, 'ground floor-to-soffit'). The podium screen above it carries no floor lines - S2 measures its four 3.75 m bands as a facade rhythm, 'NOT floor lines'. The 23 residential lines start at the podium roof, 19.40 m (S2 H_POD = 5 * FLOOR * 1.19, five podium levels each about 1.19x a residential floor), and run to 91.12; the 24th line is the roof at 94.38 (S2 H_TOP, ROWS = 23). 5 podium levels + 23 residential + the L29 pavilion = the 29 floors S1 and S3 both carry.
levels._heights_src: S2: H_POD 19.40 + 23 x 3.26 = 94.38 to the roof, plus a 2.0 m solid dark crown band (S2 CROWN, drawn here as the parapet) = 96.38; the L29 grill pavilion stands on the central bar to 98.93 (S2 PAV_H 4.0 + PAV_SLAB 0.55). S1's 97.5 m is Overture's guess and it is OVERRIDDEN: it falls between our parapet at 96.4 and the pavilion roof at 98.9, which is exactly where a LiDAR-style high point for this building should fall, so it is consistent rather than contradictory. S3 already overrides the same 97.5 to 94.4.

colours._src: day hex; golden and night follow js/westcampus.js's ramp() unless a full trio is given. Every hex is a material albedo from S2, which sampled them off the owner's own reference photographs and traced SVG; the S2 constant is named beside each one.

clad._src: S2 TEX.cladU / MAT.cladU: '#2c2b30 field (vertical ribs)' - the dark corrugated cladding the whole outer facade sits on, sampled from simeondraw.svg per S2 audit 4.1

panel._src: DERIVED, not sampled: the light boxed window surround is two S2 materials - frameBase #94999d (0.147 of the cell visible) and strip #c3c4c9 (0.237) - and this generator has one tone per bay strip, so this is their area-weighted blend, 177/180/184. S3's own distant read of the same cell (#6f7172 over field+frame+glass) is the check: ours averages #666a6b across the wall, one step darker because S3 blended a lighter frame.

strip._src: S2 MAT.strip: 'light accent strips'. Used here as the window reveal tone, which is what puts the light edge round every opening.

glassU._src: S2 MAT.glassU: 'window glass - matte olive per swatch, low reflection so it doesn't go teal under sky'

courtPanel._src: S2 TEX.courtPanel / audit 4.5: 'Panel albedo ~#a0a3a6. An earlier read said #c3c4c9 - that was anchored on a CLIPPED 255 pixel'. The court's bar faces.

courtFlute._src: S2 TEX.courtFlute: 'the wing inner faces are a DEEPLY FLUTED silver metal'

podFin._src: S2 TEX.podFin: 'the albedo is NEUTRAL #2c2d33 - the warm taupe every previous read baked in was GOLDEN-HOUR LIGHT, not material. It is the same value as the tower's dark cladding.'

podReveal._src: S2 MAT.podReveal - the light reveal line at each of the screen's band joints

podCoping._src: S2 MAT.podCoping - the cap on the screen at the podium roof

sfGlass._src: S2 MAT.sfGlass - the recessed ground-floor storefront glazing

sfFrame._src: S2 MAT.sfFrame - dark bronze storefront mullions

pavConc._src: S2 MAT.pavConc - the pavilion's exposed concrete, and the court loggia's square columns

pavShade._src: DERIVED: the open colonnade at L29 reads as a shadowed void behind the piers. Entered as the darkest neutral in S2's pavilion set (between MAT.archPanel #16181b and MAT.courtHead #14161a, lifted for ambient) rather than sampled.

crown._src: S2 MAT.parapet - 'solid dark band on every roofline'

colours._roof_src: S2 TEX.roof base #9a9a98; golden and night entered the way the other files enter a top face
colours._deckTone_src: S2 TEX.courtPav '#e3ded2 white court pavers' - the podium roof is the two court terraces

equip._src: S2 MAT.equip - roof plant, ducts and the pavilion's louvre screen

poolPaver._src: S2 TEX.poolPaver - the 600 mm terrazzo checkerboard alternates clay #cdb09c and cream #e6ded2; one tone here is their midpoint

loungeWhite._src: S2 MAT.loungeWhite - pool coping, roof pads, white furniture

chaiseWhite._src: S2 MAT.chaiseWhite - the moulded in-water chaises

planterWhite._src: S2 MAT.planterWhite - the bright concrete planter rims and the roof penthouse

planterDark._src: S2 MAT.planterDark - planter soil and condenser chassis

plant._src: S2 MAT.shrubGreen - the clumped planting mass

lawn._src: S2 MAT.lawn - the court terrace turf

deckWood._src: S2 TEX.wood, its median plank - the court terrace's wood strip and pergola platform

colours._jumbo_src: S2's jumbotron material (colour 0x1a2a4a with emissive 0x2244aa); the night value is the emissive, so the screen stays lit after dark

skins._src: one rule per face treatment; every count comes from a module, never a hard-coded number

mod4._src: The outer facade, all four sides of both wings. S2's 'mod-4' wall: a SQUARE 3.26 m cell on the dark clad field, each cell carrying a light boxed surround 0.79 of the cell wide and tall, two light strips, and a 0.49-cell window - 'Light box 0.79 of cell, glass 0.49, light strip 0.15, edge inset ~0.105; these sum to 1.0 exactly.' Here the box is a 2.58 m bay strip and the 0.68 m dark reveal shows on all four sides of it: the vertical reveal from the bay module, the horizontal one from `floorLine`. The window is 1.60 x 1.60 with its light `strip` reveal, sill 1.17 above the floor line so the cell is centred. The bay divides the faces into S2's own frozen counts with nothing rounded: the 52.01 m long faces give 16 columns and the 22.82 m end caps give 7, which are 'Simeon's counts - VERIFIED CORRECT, do not change'. What is NOT reproduced is the k=(c-r) mod 4 pairing that merges half the cells into horizontal and half into vertical two-cell dominoes; see `open`.

court._src: The two court back walls - the central bar's north and south faces. S2 audit 4.5, after three of its own refutations: 'Uniform primitive, one centred punched window per bay per floor, no pairing, no boxed surround', bay/floor = 0.941 'measured in-plane so it is perspective-immune', window 0.514 of the bay by 0.534 of the floor. 3.07 m bay across a 31.41 m wall gives 10 columns.

flank._src: The wings' inner flanks, the long walls of both courts. S2 audit 4.5 'SETTLED Jul 29': not the bar's punched grid but 'a UNIFORM WIDE 4-LIGHT RIBBON, 2.09 x FLOOR wide by 0.65 x FLOOR tall (6.8 x 2.1 m) - about 30% taller than the bar face's window, so it is a genuinely different system', repeating at 2.40 x FLOOR. The four lights inside one ribbon are not drawn - three mullions at 1.7 m spacing are under a pixel at this app's oblique camera. The deep silver fluting is drawn flat for the reason the Castilian file's fin screen is: a 0.5 m rib at this camera is a moire barcode, not a material.

flankBlank._src: The blank fluted return at each re-entrant corner, where the flank meets the bar - S2: 'a BLANK fluted return of 1-2 bays at each re-entrant corner'. 8.6 m = 2.8 bar-bays, S2's own figure.

loggia._src: Level 6, the bottom of the court: S2 audit 4.5 (C) - 'the court has 22 rows to the outer faces' 23, because L6 is a full-height GLAZED LOGGIA recessed ~1 bay behind the tower face, on square columns. That recess IS the change on the way down.' Square columns 0.56 m at the 3.07 m bay on the face line, the soffit band 0.34 m, dark court glass behind. The 3.3 m recess itself is not modelled - see `open`; the 0.45 m reveal is as far back as this generator sets a pane.

screen._src: The podium above the ground floor: S2 audit 6 'REBUILT Jul 29' - 'ONE RECESSED GLAZED GROUND FLOOR under an OVERSAILING SCREENED BOX'. 'The screen is one material with no openings anywhere; the band rhythm is a facade rhythm, NOT floor lines': ground floor-to-soffit 4.4 m, then four equal 3.75 m bands to the podium roof at 19.40, a 0.22 m light reveal on each band line and a 0.30 m coping at the top. The vertical fins themselves (S2 podFin: 105 mm pitch, 12 fins per 1.25 m panel) are NOT drawn: at 0.105 m they are a twentieth of a pixel at this app's oblique camera and a fraction of one at walking height, and the Castilian file's fin screen is the precedent for what a sub-pixel stripe does to a wall. The 1.25 m panel bay is kept as the module.

ground._src: The ground floor: S2 audit 6 - 'dark bronze storefront on 1.56 m mullion bays with a transom at 0.76 of its height, set back INSET behind the screen line'. INSET is 2.4 m in S2; this generator has no per-band inset, so the wall is in the podium plane with the panes 0.5 m back - the deepest reveal that does not turn the reveal strips into walls. See `open`. The round exposed-concrete columns on the screen line are not drawn.

colonnade._src: The L29 grill pavilion's open south side: S2 audit 5.5 - 'an open-sided concrete colonnade spanning the full building width, roofed by a slab that oversails the column line', square 0.60 m piers on ~5.7 m bays, one ceiling fan per bay. Drawn as a storefront whose glass is the shadowed void behind the piers.

pavWall._src: The pavilion's enclosed core - S2: 'Everything NORTH of it is the enclosed core/back-of-house, a SOLID volume up to the plant deck'

blocks._src: The whole site, grade to the L6 roof deck: S2's POD, five levels, 'a podium apron (full footprint)'. The traced outline IS this apron (see _massing_src).
blocks._plan_src: the obb rectangle, not the ring: the footprint is a rectangle (S1) and obbOf reports it as 80.05 x 55.01. Entered as a rectangle for the reason the Castilian file gives - clipWall only splits a wall it can prove is axis-parallel, and a traced ring carries a fraction of a degree of numerical tilt.
blocks._parapet_src: the screen's own coping, standing 0.45 m proud of the deck; S2 draws it as podCoping at H_POD - 0.30, 0.34 tall, and the terrace guard bands at the two court openings are separate (see `deck`)

blocks._src: The WEST wing, the elevation toward the Mark. S2: solid(MAT.darkRib, WW.x0, H_POD, WW.z0, WW.x1, H_TOP, WW.z1), 'WEST wing (full depth)' - 7 modules wide, the full 16-module depth, 23 rows. Its u1 face is the 16-column mod-4 long wall S2 calls 'the finalized 16 x 23 mod-4 wall'; v0 and v1 are the 7-column end caps.

faces._src: the one face of this wing that looks into the courts wears the loggia and the ribbon flank; the other three are the outer mod-4 wall. u0 is the east-facing flank of the WEST wing.

overrides._src: the blank fluted return at the north court's re-entrant corner, 8.60 m = 2.8 bar-bays (S2)
the same return at the south court's re-entrant corner

blocks._parapet_src: S2 CROWN = 2.0, 'solid dark crown band (single height)', drawn by band() on every roofline edge in MAT.parapet

S2 PLANTERS: 'RECTILINEAR planters - long bars, L-hooks and a big lightning-Z - each with a BRIGHT concrete rim around dark planting', spread over the north part of the deck. Drawn as the long-bar member of that vocabulary; the L and Z shapes are not.
the clumped planting inside those rims (S2 plantBed)

S2: the bright roof plant enclosure on the wing roof north of the bar
S2 condenser(): a dark chassis 1.15 x 2.0 x 0.78 with a brighter fan deck; S2 puts DENSE GRIDS of them on the wing roofs north of the bar and on the pavilion's plant deck

faces._src: the one face of this wing that looks into the courts wears the loggia and the ribbon flank; the other three are the outer mod-4 wall. u1 is the west-facing flank of the EAST wing.

the same return at the south court's re-entrant corner

S2: box(MAT.loungeWhite, ...) - the pale coping the pool sits in

S2: the pool, a reverse-L of deep water with a large 1-ft sun shelf, read off the Greystar nadir 20475PL3 'effectively a dimensioned plan'. Drawn as one rectangle of water; the shelf and the ten in-water chaises are not.
S2: 'deck chaises: TWO staggered columns' east of the pool
S2: three grey modular sofas along the south edge

blocks._src: The central connecting bar - S2: solid(MAT.darkRib, CX0, H_POD, BAR.z0, CX1, H_TOP, BAR.z1), the 5 middle modules of the 6+5+5 N-S split. Its two long faces are the court back walls.
blocks._plan_src: u from the wings' inner faces; v = S2's BAR = modules 6..11 of 16, here 21.00 to 37.26. The N-S band split is modular: 6 (north court) + 5 (bar) + 5 (south court) = 16.

faces._src: u0 and u1 stand against the two wings - never drawn (docs/apartments.md: a face that stands against another block). v0 faces north into the north court and v1 south into the south court; both are the punched grid over the L6 loggia.

blocks._parapet_src: only the two court edges - the u edges are inside the wings, whose own parapets already stand there

blocks._src: The L29 covered grill pavilion, standing on the bar. S2 audit 5.5: 'NOT a free-standing pergola and NOT on Level 6: it is the SOUTH FACE OF THE NORTH BAR at Level 29 - an open-sided concrete colonnade spanning the full building width, roofed by a slab that oversails the column line, with the mechanical plant sitting on TOP of that slab behind a ribbed louvre screen.' Proven there two ways: the Hill Country horizon at eye level in the interior panoramas, and the crown aerial photographing it from outside above the parapet.

faces._src: v1 is the SOUTH face - 'The room OPENS SOUTH, onto the pool deck and sky garden', so it is the open colonnade; the other three are the enclosed core's concrete.

roofItems._src: S2: the ribbed louvre screen round the plant deck on top of the pavilion slab
S2: 'DENSE GRIDS of condensers in four clusters' on the plant deck
S2: box(MAT.planterWhite, ... 9.0, 2.3, 5.0) - the penthouse over the middle of the plant deck

deck._src: The podium roof at 19.40 is the L6 amenity level, and what stands on it is the two court terraces - S2's 'COURT TERRACE on the podium roof, south court' and 'north court: quieter planted terrace'.

S2: the organic lawn in the middle of the south court, drawn as its rectangle
S2: plane(MAT.deckWood) - the wood strip down the west side of the court
S2: the first of the twin spas, its white surround
S2: the dark mast carrying the jumbotron over the turf ('turf courtyard with jumbotron', the leasing site)
S2: the jumbotron screen itself, emissive so it reads at night
S2: box(MAT.parapet, ... 1.4 ...) - the guard band across the south court's open end
S2: the same court pavers over the north court
S2: the row of six planters with trees across the north court's terrace, drawn as one continuous bed
S2: three white benches near the north court's south end
S2: the guard band across the north court's open end, on to W 24th St

open: The k=(c-r) mod 4 PAIRING is not drawn. S2's outer wall merges every cell into a two-cell domino - k0 with the cell to its right (horizontal, with horizontally-ribbed cladding behind it), k3 with the cell below (vertical) - so half the vertical reveals and half the horizontal ones vanish in a diagonal weave, and the pattern index is continued around the corners so the diagonals wrap on to the end caps. This generator has no per-cell rule, so every cell here is a single: the module, the counts, the window size and the tone statistics are S2's, the weave is not. Adding it would be a fifth skin kind ('mod4') in js/slopes-apartments.js taking a period and a pairing table. TODO for the generator.

The court is 31.41 m wide here and 36.45 m in S2, because the traced footprint is 5 m narrower E-W than S2's photograph chain (see _massing_src). The visible cost is the court back wall: 10 bays where S2 counted 12 in its reference photographs. A dimensioned plan, or a nadir rectified the way The Standard's was, would settle which is right.

The ground floor is drawn in the podium plane. In S2 it is recessed 2.4 m behind the screen line, on round exposed-concrete columns that carry the oversail; the generator has no per-band inset, so the panes sit 0.5 m back and the columns are not drawn. Same todo as The Castilian's ground floor.

The L6 court loggia is likewise flush: S2 recesses its glazing 3.3 m behind the tower face, which is the single move that makes the court 'change on the way down'. Here it is the colonnade skin in the wall plane.

The podium's vertical fins (0.105 m pitch) and the court flanks' deep fluting (about 0.5 m) are drawn as flat tone. Both are at or under a pixel at this app's cameras, and the Castilian file records what a regular sub-pixel stripe does to a wall: moire arcs the reference does not have.

S2's roof and deck kit is drawn as boxes: the pool is one rectangle rather than its reverse-L with the sun shelf, the planters are long bars rather than S2's L, hook and lightning-Z vocabulary, and the furniture, pots, trees, ceiling fans, grill islands and breeze-block screen are not there. Everything above 94 m is seen from a long way off in this app.
No balconies and no sign. S2's audit header says of this building's decks: 'NO SIGN', and the mod-4 wall is flush - there is no balcony module anywhere in S2.
The east and west wings are drawn identical, as S2 draws them ('mirrored onto the east wing, Simeon-confirmed'). Nothing here has checked that against a photograph of the Rio Grande elevation.
